page.layout: One page of text in a single column. A marginal note in the right margin, beside the text of the third paragraph. Signature "E iij" at the foot.

main_text.p: hominum mensura implebitur atque absolve-tur: nullaque post eum diem afflictio erit pio-rum, sed omnes lachrymæ abstergentur ab ocu-lis omnium,Apocal.21.4.

Occupavit enim]Hactenus intentata sunt quasi adversus Judæos iftos obftinatos crimina: nunc pronunciatur adversus eosdē sententia gravis. Senfus verborum eft: Jampridem occupavit eos ira Dei, sed ira hæc ipsis incumbet tantisper dū penitus ab eâ absorbeantur. Sic adversus eos denunciatur impletio & confummatio iræ illius, quę jampridem eos cœpit occupare: quem-admodum ipsi non cessant peccare, tantisper dum impleant & consumment[?] peccata sua. Notandum, quòd hæc verba contineant rationem superiorum. Nam ideo non faciunt peccandi fi-nè, quòd ira Dei eos occupet ad extremum usque.

Ut enim misericordia Dei, quæ nos quasi irradi-at, causa est cur bene agamus in vitâ istâ: sic ira Dei nobis imminens, causa quędâ est cur pecce-mus. Qui enim deseritur[?] à Deo, necesse est pec-cet: Augescente autem peccato, augescit ira illa; quæ est peccati quędam causa. Est enim & causa quędam, & effectû: peccati quidē {*}simpliciterScilicet con-fiderati., est causa; peccati vero aucti, est effectum. Sic simul implentur peccata & ira Dei, & quasi fervatâ quadâ proportione thesaurizantur in diē iræ & manifestationis justi judicii Dei: Quo demum die impletum peccatū punietur per impletam iram. Cum peccato augescente & irâ Dei thesaurizatâ simul sunt divitiæ illæ bonitatis, lenitatis, & tole-

page.notes: Long s throughout normalised to s (e.g. "mensura", "post", "sed", "ipsi"), as the rule requires. Hyphens at line ends kept as printed. The first word of the note is in italic; the note is printed in two lines, joined here as "Scilicet con-fiderati." The mark "*" before "simpliciter" is printed as an asterisk and is treated as a reference mark. Doubtful readings: "consumment" (the printed letters are unclear), "deseritur" (the letter after d is unclear, read as long s with a possible f), and "auctì" read as "aucti" with a ct ligature. "quem-admodum" keeps the printed line-end hyphen. The line-end "fi-nè" has an accent on e as printed.
